name: Treble Cone
locality: Above the Matukituki Valley road, near Wānaka
operator: Treble Cone Investments Ltd, owned by Cardrona Alpine Resort (RealNZ group); Cardrona & Treble Cone brand

source.note: Piste reference data — confirm at source. Approximate ski-area base position (no village; visitors stay in Wānaka)

Official Lift Passes page (read 2026-10-03): "Treble Cone is famous for its steeps, with a 4km longest run, a lift elevation of 1960m, and a 700m vertical". Base 1,260 m is from an earlier search summary (1,960 − 700).

Search summary: 550 hectares (kept in this note). The same summary gave '59 trails accessed by 8 lifts, including gondolas, high-speed quads and surface lifts'; Treble Cone is not known to have a gondola (reference), so the trail and lift counts are left unknown pending confirmation. Season id 2025-26.
Piste reference data — confirm at source. Only features Piste is confident about are set; everything else is unknown (null), not 'not offered'.

character: A big, steep ski area above Lake Wānaka with the largest lift-served vertical in the Queenstown Southern Lakes district (about 700 m). Its terrain is known for advanced and freeride skiing, and it is run together with Cardrona.
learning: Reference note: Treble Cone has a small learner area and snowsports school, but most terrain suits confident skiers; confirm 2027 lesson products.

source.note: Winter 2026: published season dates 27 Jun – 27 Sep 2026; the 2026 closing-dates list gives Treble Cone's close as 27 Sep 2026. The opening is the scheduled date — whether it opened on time in a delayed NZ season is not confirmed.
Winter 2025 published season dates: 28 Jun – 28 Sep 2025 (scheduled dates; actual days may have differed).

season.typicalText: Usually late June to late September (27 Jun – 27 Sep 2026; 28 Jun – 28 Sep 2025).
season.notes: Southern Hemisphere: Piste season id 2026-27 is the June–October 2027 winter (the one the 2026-27 Ikon and Epic passes cover); 2025-26 is the 2026 winter and 2024-25 the 2025 winter. No 2027 opening or closing date was found as of 2026-09-30 (NZSki's 2027 3 Peak Pass was still listed as 'Coming Soon' — https://www.theremarkables.co.nz/passes-packages/). OnTheSnow labels the 2026 NZ winter '2026/2027', so its 'projected' dates describe winter 2026, not 2027. Treble Cone is not on the Ikon or Epic 2026-27 rosters in the shared notes.
